questions.question: Determine the values of \(p\) such that the rank of \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&-1&0\\4&4&-3&1\\p&2&2&2\\9&9&p&3\end{bmatrix}\) is 3.

paragraphs: For a \(4\times4\) matrix to have rank \(3\), its determinant must be zero, but at least one third-order minor must be non-zero.
Check that the rank does not fall below 3 for these values.
For \(p=2\), the third-order minor formed by rows \(1,2,3\) and columns \(1,3,4\) is
Hence for \(p=2\), rank \(\ge3\); since \(\det A=0\), rank \(\le3\). Thus rank \(=3\).
For \(p=-6\), the third-order minor formed by rows \(1,2,3\) and columns \(1,2,3\) is
Hence for \(p=-6\), rank \(\ge3\); and again \(\det A=0\), so rank \(=3\).
answer.book_check: Printed appendix answer: “No value of \(p\) is possible.”
answer.note: Independent verification: \(\det A=-(p-2)(p+6)\). At both \(p=2\) and \(p=-6\), the matrix has rank exactly 3. Therefore the printed appendix answer “No value of \(p\) is possible” is incorrect for the matrix printed in the question.

questions.question: Investigate for consistency of the equations \(4x-2y+6z=8,\;x+y-3z=-1,\;15x-3y+9z=21\), and if possible find the solution.

answer.result: The system is consistent and \(x=1,\;y=3k-2,\;z=k\), where \(k\) is arbitrary.
answer.book_check: Printed appendix answer: Consistent; \(x=1,\;y=3k-2,\;z=k\) for all \(k\).
paragraphs: The coefficient and augmented matrices have the same rank, \(2<3\), so the system is consistent with infinitely many solutions.
Let \(z=k\). The second row gives \(y-3z=-2\), so \(y=3k-2\). The first row then gives \(x=1\).

questions.question: Find the values of \(a,b\) for which the equations \(x+ay+z=3,\;x+2y+2z=b,\;x+5y+3z=9\) are consistent. When will these equations have a unique solution?

answer.result: Consistent for \(a\ne-1\) with any \(b\), and also for \(a=-1,b=6\). The solution is unique when \(a\ne-1\); for \(a=-1,b=6\) there are infinitely many solutions.
answer.book_check: Printed appendix answer: for \(a=-1,b=6\), the equations are consistent and have infinitely many solutions; for \(a\ne-1\), \(b\) may have any value and the solution is unique.
paragraphs: Therefore, if \(a\ne-1\), then \(|A|\ne0\), so the system has a unique solution for every value of \(b\).
Consistency requires \(12-2b=0\), hence \(b=6\). For \(a=-1,b=6\), the rank is \(2<3\), so there are infinitely many solutions.

answer.book_check: Printed appendix answer: (i) \(\lambda=3,\mu\ne10\); (ii) \(\lambda\ne3\); (iii) \(\lambda=3,\mu=10\).

If \(\lambda=3\), the last row becomes \([0\;0\;0\mid\mu-10]\). Thus \(\mu\ne10\) gives a contradiction and no solution, whereas \(\mu=10\) gives a zero row and infinitely many solutions.

questions.question: Show that if \(\lambda\ne-5\), the system \(3x-y+4z=3,\;x+2y-3z=-2,\;6x+5y+\lambda z=-3\) has a unique solution. If \(\lambda=-5\), show that the equations are consistent. Determine the solutions in each case.

answer.book_check: Printed appendix answer agrees: for \(\lambda\ne-5\), \(x=4/7,y=-9/7,z=0\); for \(\lambda=-5\), \(x=(4-5k)/7,y=(13k-9)/7,z=k\).
paragraphs: Interchange the first two rows and row-reduce:
If \(\lambda\ne-5\), then \(z=0\). Row 2 gives \(-7y=9\), so \(y=-9/7\). Row 1 gives \(x+2(-9/7)=-2\), hence \(x=4/7\).
If \(\lambda=-5\), the last row is zero. Put \(z=k\). Row 2 gives \(y=(13k-9)/7\). Row 1 gives \(x=(4-5k)/7\). Thus the system is consistent with infinitely many solutions.

questions.question: Find the values of \(\lambda\) for which the equations \((2-\lambda)x+2y+3=0,\;2x+(4-\lambda)y+7=0,\;2x+5y+(6-\lambda)=0\) are consistent, and find the values of \(x,y\) corresponding to each value of \(\lambda\).

answer.book_check: Printed appendix answer: \(\lambda=-1,1,12\), with \(x=-1/11,y=-15/11\); \(x=-5,y=1\); \(x=1/2,y=1\), respectively.
paragraphs: Write the system in augmented form, with right-hand sides \(-3,-7,\lambda-6\):
For three equations in two unknowns to be consistent, the three rows of the augmented \(3\times3\) matrix must be linearly dependent. Hence its determinant must vanish:
For \(\lambda=-1\), the first two equations are \(3x+2y=-3\), \(2x+5y=-7\). Solving gives \(x=-1/11,y=-15/11\).
For \(\lambda=1\), the first two equations are \(x+2y=-3\), \(2x+3y=-7\). Solving gives \(x=-5,y=1\).
For \(\lambda=12\), the first two equations are \(-10x+2y=-3\), \(2x-8y=-7\). Solving gives \(x=1/2,y=1\).
In each case the third equation is also satisfied.
